egress.terms: not stated for the free tier: the plan card lists no traffic volume and no bandwidth figure

interface_detail: 'Console Access' on every plan; the blog announcement adds 'Management: Web-Based Console Access + Direct SSH'. Full root access is stated for the micro instances generally.
tooling: any SSH client; the vendor's panel; a one-click app catalogue including Docker, Tailscale, WG-Easy and Uptime Kuma
chaining: a small always-on IPv6 container with a console, a renew-every-30-days clock and no card, which suits a monitor or a low-traffic IPv6 service rather than anything needing inbound IPv4

limits.value: the free container must be renewed every 30 days to confirm active use

a stock window the vendor sets: the served markup marks the free plan out of stock until 2026-10-29 with the order button disabled, and the page's script re-enables the button after that time; the matching server-side setting (FREE_MICRO_OUT_OF_STOCK_UNTIL) is not published

binding_note: the free plan is gated by a stock window the vendor sets and has moved (a markup comment reads 2026-10-21, the notice and the script read 2026-10-29); after 2026-10-29 the page's script offers 'Claim Free Server', and whether the server accepts a free order is behind a sign-in

identity_cost.detail: The register form asks for a full name, an email, a password and a Terms checkbox, with Google and Discord sign-in offered as alternatives; an order placed while signed out is sent to that sign-in page. The page's checkout script handles a free order with no payment step ('The free instance is never charged.') and sends it to card payment only when the +$4/mo Shared IPv4 (NAT) add-on is chosen. No phone and no document appears on any page read.

reliability_note: the vendor's home page states '99.8%+' uptime for its services, and the free plan card states 'No formal uptime agreement.'; the free plan has been out of stock for stretches the vendor…

notes: The vendor's blog announcement and its live plan card disagree on the free shape: the blog says 2 vCPU and 2 GB, the card says 1 vCPU and 512 MB. The card is the page served at the point of sale, so the record uses the card and the disagreement is written down rather than resolved. The free plan is gated by a stock window the vendor sets and has moved (a markup comment reads 2026-10-21, the notice and script read 2026-10-29); the page's script re-opens the order button after 2026-10-29. The checkout script handles a free order with no payment step unless the paid shared IPv4 add-on is chosen. Not established: the traffic allowance, and whether the server accepts a free order after the stock window.
